items.title: One place word, several English readings
items.caption: The Samoan place word stays *i*. The verb and the place determine whether English reads it as in, to, or into.

cells.sm: Sā nofo le pusi i le laau.
cells.en: The cat stayed in the tree.

cells.sm: Sā ia alu i le fale.
Sā oso le pusi i le laau.
cells.en: The cat jumped into the tree.

items.title: The end phrase points to or from
items.caption: The place word points to a destination or location. The from-word marks where the movement started.

states.label: To a place
states.sm: Sā ia alu i le fale.

states.label: From a place
states.sm: Na sau le tama mai le fale.
states.en: The boy came from the house.

items.title: Sort the place phrases by their job
items.intro: Sort each complete printed sentence by whether its last phrase marks a location, a destination, or a source.

items.sm: Sā nofo le tama i le fale.
items.en: The boy stayed in the house.
items.why: With a verb of staying, *i* sets the action in a place.

items.sm: Sā ʻou alu i le nuʻu.
items.why: With a verb of movement, *i* points toward the destination.

items.sm: Sā oso le pusi i le laau.
items.en: The cat jumped into the tree.
items.why: The movement enters the destination, so English reads *i* as into.

items.sm: Na sau le teine mai le nuʻu.
items.en: The girl came from the village.
items.why: The from-word *mai* marks where the movement started.

items.sm: Na oso le pusi mai le laau.
items.en: The cat jumped from the tree.
items.why: The from-word points away from the source.
